title: Inclusion of the uniform finite-Tor integral domain
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$, the integral constructible category consists of the derived-complete constructible complexes [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and its uniform finite-Tor full subcategory is that of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Define its inclusion into the integral constructible category by forgetting the finite-Tor condition: it retains the same underlying complex and morphism. In the finite-field setting $D$ with $\ell\ne D.p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the coefficient-prime unit witness is the canonical proof that the image of $\ell$ in $D.k$ is nonzero, hence a unit, since $D.k$ has characteristic $D.p$. This fixes the proof argument of the recorded compact-support functor without adding a new invertibility hypothesis.
